observation.transcript: The Crimson Hexagon archive is a historical data repository of more than one trillion public social media posts.Archive OverviewScale: The database held over 1 trillion posts collected globally from networks like Twitter, Facebook, Instagram, and Tumblr, alongside blogs and forums.Timeframe: It indexed public conversations and media, tracking data scaling back across multiple years for sentiment analysis and trend tracking.Users: Brands, academic groups like Pew Research, and various agencies used the platform for consumer insights and public opinion research.Regulatory Scrutiny2018 Suspension: Facebook temporarily suspended the company's access amid investigations into how public data was analyzed for government and non-profit contracts.Resolution: Reviews found that the firm relied strictly on publicly available data rather than scraping private user profiles, and platform access was largely restored.If you want, let me know:Are you looking for technical documentation on how their data platform worked?Do you need information on their merger and corporate history?I can provide more specific details.crimson hexagonal archiveThe Crimson Hexagonal Archive is an expansive, decentralized digital preservation project and literature initiative created by independent scholar and poet Lee Sharks. It explores theme-driven concepts like "semantic autonomy," structural data compression, and how human meaning survives platform coercion and algorithmic flattening.1. Literary & Theoretical RootsThe archive takes its name and structural inspiration from Jorge Luis Borges' famous 1941 short story The Library of Babel. In the story, the "Crimson Hexagon" refers to a mythical, elusive room housing all-powerful, magical, and perfect compendia of books. Sharks uses this framework to explore how to architect a repository where texts are structured as "meaning-objects" designed to withstand external digital erosion.2. The 2026 Zenodo Deletion & RestructuringThe project gained significant attention following a major platform dispute:The Removal: On June 19, 2026, the European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN) terminated the depositing account hosting the archive on the Zenodo repository. This sudden action instantly removed 862 works and disrupted 1,817 Digital Object Identifiers (DOIs).The "Sovereign" Pivot: Rather than dissolving, the archive was reconstructed using alternate tracking protocols and an independent restoration index mapping 1,937 identifiers. Its very first deposit post-deletion—Zenodotus' Book-Burning: Loud Exclusion at Repository Scale—formally documented the deletion event itself as a piece of performance archive.3. Core Structural ElementsThe database operates under its own complex, self-referential worldbuilding mechanics:The Fractal Navigation Map (FNM): A self-similar design architecture where every localized piece of documentation contains the core coding and logical layout of the entire network.The Space Ark: A formalized data-compression initiative (EA-ARK-01) meant to preserve heavy analytical formulas and philosophical preprints under strict structural guidelines.Collaborative Imprints: Sub-deposits include niche structural bodies like Maybe Space Baby Garden Lanes (MSBGL) and the Journal of Forensic Semiotics, which house music, audio-visual poetry, and essays on platform economy diagnostics.If you want to delve deeper into a specific layer of the project, let me know if you would like:An overview of the philosophical texts contained within it (like the Moving Statues Made of Rubies Mint).Technical details regarding how its DOI recovery indexes and SPXI Protocols operate.ZenodoThe Inauguration of Memography — Crimson Hexagon Archive - ZenodoFeb 23, 2026 — Description (copy-paste to Zenodo description field).
